text:
Canoe upriver,

canoe downriver.

The rich man lives off the poor

and the poor man off his work.


The fisherman fishes

what he cannot

and keeps checking

the longlines.


Canoe upriver,

canoe downriver,

he starves

with his work.


The fisherman fishes

what he does not want:

his misery of children

dying on him.


Canoe upriver,

canoe downriver.

The rich man lives off the poor

and the poor man off his work.


And here a period must be put:

the woman suffers it

for all of them together.

translation.title: Canoe
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the river-song refrain and the economic critique of fishing labor and family suffering.
